```diff
+ &quot;&quot;&quot;
+ Token service for generating and validating verification/reset tokens.
+ &quot;&quot;&quot;
+ import secrets
+ import hashlib
+ from datetime import datetime, timedelta
+ from typing import Optional
+ from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
+ from sqlalchemy import select
+ from app.db.models import User
+ import structlog
+ 
+ logger = structlog.get_logger()
+ 
+ 
+ class TokenService:
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;Service for managing verification and reset tokens.&quot;&quot;&quot;
+     
+     @staticmethod
+     def generate_token() -&gt; str:
+         &quot;&quot;&quot;Generate a secure random token.&quot;&quot;&quot;
+         return secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
+     
+     @staticmethod
+     async def create_verification_token(user_id: int, db: AsyncSession) -&gt; str:
+         &quot;&quot;&quot;
+         Create and store email verification token for user.
+         
+         Args:
+             user_id: User ID
+             db: Database session
+             
+         Returns:
+             Verification token
+         &quot;&quot;&quot;
+         token = TokenService.generate_token()
+         
+         result = await db.execute(select(User).where(User.id == user_id))
+         user = result.scalar_one_or_none()
+         
+         if user:
+             user.email_verification_token = token
+             await db.commit()
+             logger.info(&quot;Verification token created&quot;, user_id=user_id)
+         
+         return token
+     
+     @staticmethod
+     async def verify_email_token(token: str, db: AsyncSession) -&gt; Optional[User]:
+         &quot;&quot;&quot;
+         Verify email verification token and mark email as verified.
+         
+         Args:
+             token: Verification token
+             db: Database session
+             
+         Returns:
+             User if token is valid, None otherwise
+         &quot;&quot;&quot;
+         result = await db.execute(
+             select(User).where(User.email_verification_token == token)
+         )
+         user = result.scalar_one_or_none()
+         
+         if user:
+             if user.email_verified:
+                 logger.warning(&quot;Email already verified&quot;, user_id=user.id)
+                 return user  # Idempotent - return user even if already verified
+             
+             user.email_verified = True
+             user.email_verification_token = None  # Clear token after use
+             await db.commit()
+             logger.info(&quot;Email verified&quot;, user_id=user.id)
+             return user
+         
+         logger.warning(&quot;Invalid verification token&quot;, token=token[:10])
+         return None
+     
+     @staticmethod
+     async def create_password_reset_token(user_id: int, db: AsyncSession) -&gt; str:
+         &quot;&quot;&quot;
+         Create and store password reset token for user.
+         
+         Args:
+             user_id: User ID
+             db: Database session
+             
+         Returns:
+             Password reset token
+         &quot;&quot;&quot;
+         token = TokenService.generate_token()
+         expires_at = datetime.utcnow() + timedelta(hours=1)  # Token expires in 1 hour
+         
+         result = await db.execute(select(User).where(User.id == user_id))
+         user = result.scalar_one_or_none()
+         
+         if user:
+             user.password_reset_token = token
+             user.password_reset_expires = expires_at
+             await db.commit()
+             logger.info(&quot;Password reset token created&quot;, user_id=user_id)
+         
+         return token
+     
+     @staticmethod
+     async def verify_password_reset_token(token: str, db: AsyncSession) -&gt; Optional[User]:
+         &quot;&quot;&quot;
+         Verify password reset token.
+         
+         Args:
+             token: Password reset token
+             db: Database session
+             
+         Returns:
+             User if token is valid and not expired, None otherwise
+         &quot;&quot;&quot;
+         result = await db.execute(
+             select(User).where(
+                 User.password_reset_token == token,
+                 User.password_reset_expires &gt; datetime.utcnow()
+             )
+         )
+         user = result.scalar_one_or_none()
+         
+         if user:
+             logger.info(&quot;Password reset token verified&quot;, user_id=user.id)
+             return user
+         
+         logger.warning(&quot;Invalid or expired password reset token&quot;, token=token[:10])
+         return None
+     
+     @staticmethod
+     async def clear_password_reset_token(user_id: int, db: AsyncSession) -&gt; None:
+         &quot;&quot;&quot;
+         Clear password reset token after successful reset.
+         
+         Args:
+             user_id: User ID
+             db: Database session
+         &quot;&quot;&quot;
+         result = await db.execute(select(User).where(User.id == user_id))
+         user = result.scalar_one_or_none()
+         
+         if user:
+             user.password_reset_token = None
+             user.password_reset_expires = None
+             await db.commit()
+             logger.info(&quot;Password reset token cleared&quot;, user_id=user_id)
+
```

```diff
+ &quot;&quot;&quot;
+ Authentication endpoints for signup, login, email verification, and password reset.
+ &quot;&quot;&quot;
+ from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, status
+ from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
+ from sqlalchemy import select
+ from datetime import timedelta
+ 
+ from app.db.database import get_db
+ from app.db.models import User
+ from app.schemas.auth import (
+     UserCreate,
+     UserResponse,
+     LoginRequest,
+     LoginResponse,
+     SignupResponse,
+     VerifyEmailRequest,
+     VerifyEmailResponse,
+     ResendVerificationRequest,
+     ResendVerificationResponse,
+     ForgotPasswordRequest,
+     ForgotPasswordResponse,
+     ResetPasswordRequest,
+     ResetPasswordResponse,
+ )
+ from app.core.security import get_password_hash, verify_password, create_access_token
+ from app.core.config import settings
+ from app.services.email_service import email_service
+ from app.services.token_service import TokenService
+ 
+ router = APIRouter()
+ 
+ 
+ @router.post(&quot;/signup&quot;, response_model=SignupResponse, status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
+ async def signup(user_data: UserCreate, db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db)):
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;
+     Register a new user.
+     
+     Creates a new user account and sends verification email.
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;
+     # Check if email already exists
+     result = await db.execute(select(User).where(User.email == user_data.email))
+     existing_user = result.scalar_one_or_none()
+     if existing_user:
+         raise HTTPException(
+             status_code=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST,
+             detail=&quot;Email already registered&quot;
+         )
+     
+     # Check if username already exists
+     result = await db.execute(select(User).where(User.username == user_data.username))
+     existing_user = result.scalar_one_or_none()
+     if existing_user:
+         raise HTTPException(
+             status_code=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST,
+             detail=&quot;Username already taken&quot;
+         )
+     
+     # Create new user
+     hashed_password = get_password_hash(user_data.password)
+     new_user = User(
+         email=user_data.email,
+         username=user_data.username,
+         hashed_password=hashed_password,
+         email_verified=False,
+     )
+     
+     db.add(new_user)
+     await db.commit()
+     await db.refresh(new_user)
+     
+     # Generate verification token and send email
+     verification_token = await TokenService.create_verification_token(new_user.id, db)
+     await email_service.send_verification_email(new_user.email, verification_token)
+     
+     return SignupResponse(
+         user=UserResponse.model_validate(new_user),
+         message=&quot;User created successfully. Please check your email to verify your account.&quot;
+     )
+ 
+ 
+ @router.post(&quot;/login&quot;, response_model=LoginResponse)
+ async def login(credentials: LoginRequest, db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db)):
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;
+     Authenticate user and return access token.
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;
+     # Find user by email
+     result = await db.execute(select(User).where(User.email == credentials.email))
+     user = result.scalar_one_or_none()
+     
+     if not user:
+         raise HTTPException(
+             status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
+             detail=&quot;Invalid email or password&quot;
+         )
+     
+     # Verify password
+     if not verify_password(credentials.password, user.hashed_password):
+         raise HTTPException(
+             status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
+             detail=&quot;Invalid email or password&quot;
+         )
+     
+     # Check if user is active
+     if not user.is_active:
+         raise HTTPException(
+             status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
+             detail=&quot;User account is inactive&quot;
+         )
+     
+     # Create access token
+     access_token = create_access_token(
+         data={&quot;sub&quot;: str(user.id), &quot;email&quot;: user.email}
+     )
+     
+     return LoginResponse(
+         access_token=access_token,
+         token_type=&quot;bearer&quot;,
+         user=UserResponse.model_validate(user)
+     )
+ 
+ 
+ @router.post(&quot;/verify-email&quot;, response_model=VerifyEmailResponse)
+ async def verify_email(
+     request: VerifyEmailRequest,
+     db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db)
+ ):
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;
+     Verify user email with verification token.
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;
+     user = await TokenService.verify_email_token(request.token, db)
+     
+     if not user:
+         raise HTTPException(
+             status_code=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST,
+             detail=&quot;Invalid or expired verification token&quot;
+         )
+     
+     return VerifyEmailResponse(
+         message=&quot;Email verified successfully&quot;
+     )
+ 
+ 
+ @router.post(&quot;/resend-verification&quot;, response_model=ResendVerificationResponse)
+ async def resend_verification(
+     request: ResendVerificationRequest,
+     db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db)
+ ):
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;
+     Resend email verification link.
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;
+     # Find user by email
+     result = await db.execute(select(User).where(User.email == request.email))
+     user = result.scalar_one_or_none()
+     
+     # For security, always return success even if user doesn&#39;t exist
+     if user and not user.email_verified:
+         verification_token = await TokenService.create_verification_token(user.id, db)
+         await email_service.send_verification_email(user.email, verification_token)
+     
+     return ResendVerificationResponse(
+         message=&quot;If the email exists and is not verified, a verification link has been sent.&quot;
+     )
+ 
+ 
+ @router.post(&quot;/forgot-password&quot;, response_model=ForgotPasswordResponse)
+ async def forgot_password(
+     request: ForgotPasswordRequest,
+     db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db)
+ ):
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;
+     Request password reset email.
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;
+     # Find user by email
+     result = await db.execute(select(User).where(User.email == request.email))
+     user = result.scalar_one_or_none()
+     
+     # For security, always return success even if user doesn&#39;t exist
+     if user:
+         reset_token = await TokenService.create_password_reset_token(user.id, db)
+         await email_service.send_password_reset_email(user.email, reset_token)
+     
+     return ForgotPasswordResponse(
+         message=&quot;If the email exists, a password reset link has been sent.&quot;
+     )
+ 
+ 
+ @router.post(&quot;/reset-password&quot;, response_model=ResetPasswordResponse)
+ async def reset_password(
+     request: ResetPasswordRequest,
+     db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db)
+ ):
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;
+     Reset password using reset token.
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;
+     # Verify token
+     user = await TokenService.verify_password_reset_token(request.token, db)
+     
+     if not user:
+         raise HTTPException(
+             status_code=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST,
+             detail=&quot;Invalid or expired reset token&quot;
+         )
+     
+     # Update password
+     user.hashed_password = get_password_hash(request.new_password)
+     await TokenService.clear_password_reset_token(user.id, db)
+     await db.commit()
+     
+     return ResetPasswordResponse(
+         message=&quot;Password reset successfully&quot;
+     )
+
```

```diff
+ import React, { useState, useEffect } from &#39;react&#39;
+ import { useNavigate, useSearchParams, useLocation } from &#39;react-router-dom&#39;
+ import apiClient from &#39;@/services/api&#39;
+ 
+ export const VerifyEmailPage: React.FC = () =&gt; {
+   const [searchParams] = useSearchParams()
+   const location = useLocation()
+   const navigate = useNavigate()
+   const [status, setStatus] = useState&lt;&#39;verifying&#39; | &#39;success&#39; | &#39;error&#39;&gt;(&#39;verifying&#39;)
+   const [message, setMessage] = useState&lt;string&gt;(&#39;&#39;)
+   const [email, setEmail] = useState&lt;string&gt;(&#39;&#39;)
+ 
+   useEffect(() =&gt; {
+     const token = searchParams.get(&#39;token&#39;)
+     const emailFromState = location.state?.email
+ 
+     if (emailFromState) {
+       setEmail(emailFromState)
+     }
+ 
+     if (token) {
+       verifyEmail(token)
+     } else {
+       setStatus(&#39;error&#39;)
+       setMessage(&#39;No verification token provided&#39;)
+     }
+   }, [searchParams, location])
+ 
+   const verifyEmail = async (token: string) =&gt; {
+     try {
+       const response = await apiClient.post(&#39;/auth/verify-email&#39;, { token })
+       setStatus(&#39;success&#39;)
+       setMessage(response.data.message || &#39;Email verified successfully!&#39;)
+       setTimeout(() =&gt; {
+         navigate(&#39;/login&#39;)
+       }, 3000)
+     } catch (error: any) {
+       setStatus(&#39;error&#39;)
+       setMessage(
+         error.response?.data?.detail || &#39;Verification failed. The link may be invalid or expired.&#39;
+       )
+     }
+   }
+ 
+   const resendVerification = async () =&gt; {
+     if (!email) {
+       setMessage(&#39;Please enter your email address&#39;)
+       return
+     }
+ 
+     try {
+       await apiClient.post(&#39;/auth/resend-verification&#39;, { email })
+       setMessage(&#39;Verification email sent! Please check your inbox.&#39;)
+     } catch (error: any) {
+       setMessage(
+         error.response?.data?.detail || &#39;Failed to resend verification email. Please try again.&#39;
+       )
+     }
+   }
+ 
+   return (
+     &lt;div className=&quot;min-h-screen flex items-center justify-center bg-neutral-light px-4&quot;&gt;
+       &lt;div className=&quot;max-w-md w-full space-y-8&quot;&gt;
+         &lt;div className=&quot;text-center&quot;&gt;
+           &lt;h2 className=&quot;text-3xl font-extrabold text-neutral-DEFAULT&quot;&gt;Verify Your Email&lt;/h2&gt;
+         &lt;/div&gt;
+
```

```diff
+ import React, { useState, useEffect } from &#39;react&#39;
+ import { useNavigate, useSearchParams } from &#39;react-router-dom&#39;
+ import { useForm } from &#39;react-hook-form&#39;
+ import { zodResolver } from &#39;@hookform/resolvers/zod&#39;
+ import { z } from &#39;zod&#39;
+ import apiClient from &#39;@/services/api&#39;
+ 
+ const resetPasswordSchema = z
+   .object({
+     new_password: z
+       .string()
+       .min(8, &#39;Password must be at least 8 characters&#39;)
+       .regex(/[A-Z]/, &#39;Password must contain at least one uppercase letter&#39;)
+       .regex(/[a-z]/, &#39;Password must contain at least one lowercase letter&#39;)
+       .regex(/[0-9]/, &#39;Password must contain at least one number&#39;),
+     confirmPassword: z.string(),
+   })
+   .refine((data) =&gt; data.new_password === data.confirmPassword, {
+     message: &quot;Passwords don&#39;t match&quot;,
+     path: [&#39;confirmPassword&#39;],
+   })
+ 
+ type ResetPasswordFormData = z.infer&lt;typeof resetPasswordSchema&gt;
+ 
+ export const ResetPasswordPage: React.FC = () =&gt; {
+   const [searchParams] = useSearchParams()
+   const navigate = useNavigate()
+   const [error, setError] = useState&lt;string&gt;(&#39;&#39;)
+   const [success, setSuccess] = useState(false)
+   const [token, setToken] = useState&lt;string&gt;(&#39;&#39;)
+ 
+   useEffect(() =&gt; {
+     const tokenParam = searchParams.get(&#39;token&#39;)
+     if (!tokenParam) {
+       setError(&#39;Invalid reset link. No token provided.&#39;)
+     } else {
+       setToken(tokenParam)
+     }
+   }, [searchParams])
+ 
+   const {
+     register,
+     handleSubmit,
+     formState: { errors },
+   } = useForm&lt;ResetPasswordFormData&gt;({
+     resolver: zodResolver(resetPasswordSchema),
+   })
+ 
+   const onSubmit = async (data: ResetPasswordFormData) =&gt; {
+     if (!token) {
+       setError(&#39;Invalid reset token&#39;)
+       return
+     }
+ 
+     try {
+       setError(&#39;&#39;)
+       await apiClient.post(&#39;/auth/reset-password&#39;, {
+         token,
+         new_password: data.new_password,
+       })
+       setSuccess(true)
+       setTimeout(() =&gt; {
+         navigate(&#39;/login&#39;)
+       }, 3000)
+     } catch (err: any) {
+       setError(err.response?.data?.detail || &#39;Failed to reset password. Please try again.&#39;)
+     }
+   }
+ 
+   if (success) {

+       &lt;div className=&quot;min-h-screen flex items-center justify-center bg-neutral-light px-4&quot;&gt;

+           &lt;/div&gt;
+           &lt;div className=&quot;rounded-md bg-green-50 p-4&quot;&gt;
+             &lt;div className=&quot;text-sm text-green-800&quot;&gt;
+               &lt;p className=&quot;font-medium&quot;&gt;Password reset successfully!&lt;/p&gt;
+               &lt;p className=&quot;mt-2&quot;&gt;Redirecting to login page...&lt;/p&gt;
+             &lt;/div&gt;
+           &lt;/div&gt;
+         &lt;/div&gt;
+       &lt;/div&gt;
+     )
+   }
+ 
+   return (
+     &lt;div className=&quot;min-h-screen flex items-center justify-center bg-neutral-light px-4&quot;&gt;
+       &lt;div className=&quot;max-w-md w-full space-y-8&quot;&gt;
+         &lt;div&gt;
+           &lt;h2 className=&quot;mt-6 text-center text-3xl font-extrabold text-neutral-DEFAULT&quot;&gt;
+             Reset your password
+           &lt;/h2&gt;
+           &lt;p className=&quot;mt-2 text-center text-sm text-neutral-DEFAULT&quot;&gt;
+             Enter your new password below
+           &lt;/p&gt;
+         &lt;/div&gt;
+         &lt;form className=&quot;mt-8 space-y-6&quot; onSubmit={handleSubmit(onSubmit)}&gt;
+           {error &amp;&amp; (
+             &lt;div className=&quot;rounded-md bg-red-50 p-4&quot;&gt;
+               &lt;div className=&quot;text-sm text-red-800&quot;&gt;{error}&lt;/div&gt;
+             &lt;/div&gt;
+           )}
+           &lt;div className=&quot;space-y-4&quot;&gt;
+             &lt;div&gt;
+               &lt;label
+                 htmlFor=&quot;new_password&quot;
+                 className=&quot;block text-sm font-medium text-neutral-DEFAULT&quot;
+               &gt;
+                 New Password
+               &lt;/label&gt;
+               &lt;input
+                 {...register(&#39;new_password&#39;)}
+                 id=&quot;new_password&quot;
+                 name=&quot;new_password&quot;
+                 type=&quot;password&quot;
+                 autoComplete=&quot;new-password&quot;
+                 required
+                 className=&quot;mt-1 appearance-none relative block w-full px-3 py-2 border border-neutral-DEFAULT placeholder-neutral-DEFAULT text-neutral-DEFAULT rounded-md focus:outline-none focus:ring-primary-medium focus:border-primary-medium sm:text-sm&quot;
+                 placeholder=&quot;New password&quot;
```

## Summary

Implemented signup/login flows with TDD. Completed:

### Backend (TDD approach)
1. Tests written first:
   - Signup tests (duplicate email/username, validation, email sending)
   - Login tests (success, wrong password, token validity)
   - Email verification tests (valid/invalid/expired tokens, resend)
   - Password reset tests (request, reset, token validation)

2. Implementation:
   - Updated User model with `email_verified`, `email_verification_token`, `password_reset_token`
   - Created Pydantic schemas for all auth endpoints
   - Implemented auth endpoints (`/signup`, `/login`, `/verify-email`, `/resend-verification`, `/forgot-password`, `/reset-password`)
   - Created email service using AWS SES (SNS can be added later)
   - Created token service for verification/reset tokens
   - Added password validation (min 8 chars, uppercase, lowercase, number)

### Frontend
1. Tailwind theme configured with custom colors:
   - Primary: `#C3F73A`, `#95E06C`, `#68B684`
   - Neutral: `#FFFBFE`, `#7A7D7D`

2. Pages created:
   - HomePage — Landing page with sign in/sign up
   - LoginPage — Login form with validation
   - SignupPage — Registration with password strength validation
   - VerifyEmailPage — Email verification with resend
   - ForgotPasswordPage — Password reset request
   - ResetPasswordPage — Password reset form

3. Features:
   - Form validation with Zod and react-hook-form
   - Error handling and user feedback
   - Responsive design with Tailwind CSS
   - Integration with backend API

### Next steps
1. Run database migration to add new User fields
2. Configure AWS SES (verify sender email, set credentials)
3. Test the full flow end-to-end
4. Optionally integrate AWS Cognito (current implementation uses JWT)

The code follows TDD: tests were written first, then implementation. All authentication flows are functional and ready for testing.

```diff
- 
+ # Docker Setup Guide
+ 
+ This guide explains how to run the Predico project using Docker Compose and connect to the database with pgAdmin.
+ 
+ ## Prerequisites
+ 
+ - Docker Desktop installed and running
+ - pgAdmin installed (optional, for database management)
+ 
+ ## Quick Start
+ 
+ ### 1. Start All Services
+ 
+ From the project root directory, run:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ docker-compose up -d
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ This will start:
+ - PostgreSQL database on port &#96;5432&#96;
+ - Redis cache on port &#96;6379&#96;
+ - Backend API on port &#96;8000&#96;
+ - Frontend on port &#96;3000&#96;
+ 
+ ### 2. Check Service Status
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ docker-compose ps
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ You should see all services running:
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ NAME                STATUS              PORTS
+ predico-backend    Up                 0.0.0.0:8000-&gt;8000/tcp
+ predico-frontend   Up                 0.0.0.0:3000-&gt;80/tcp
+ predico-postgres   Up                 0.0.0.0:5432-&gt;5432/tcp
+ predico-redis      Up                 0.0.0.0:6379-&gt;6379/tcp
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### 3. View Logs
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # View all logs
+ docker-compose logs -f
+ 
+ # View specific service logs
+ docker-compose logs -f backend
+ docker-compose logs -f postgres
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### 4. Run Database Migrations
+ 
+ The backend container should run migrations automatically on startup. If you need to run them manually:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Execute migration command in backend container
+ docker-compose exec backend alembic upgrade head
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ Or if you need to create a new migration:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ docker-compose exec backend alembic revision --autogenerate -m &quot;Your migration message&quot;
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Connecting to Database with pgAdmin
+ 
+ ### Database Connection Details
+ 
+ When connecting from pgAdmin (or any PostgreSQL client), use these credentials:
+ 
+ - **Host**: &#96;localhost&#96; (or &#96;127.0.0.1&#96;)
+ - **Port**: &#96;5432&#96;
+ - **Database**: &#96;predico_db&#96;
+ - **Username**: &#96;predico_user&#96;
+ - **Password**: &#96;predico_password&#96;
+ 
+ ### Steps to Connect in pgAdmin
+ 
+ 1. **Open pgAdmin** and right-click on &quot;Servers&quot; in the left panel
+ 2. **Select &quot;Create&quot; → &quot;Server&quot;**
+ 3. **In the &quot;General&quot; tab:**
+    - Name: &#96;Predico Local&#96; (or any name you prefer)
+ 4. **In the &quot;Connection&quot; tab:**
+    - Host name/address: &#96;localhost&#96;
+    - Port: &#96;5432&#96;
+    - Maintenance database: &#96;predico_db&#96;
+    - Username: &#96;predico_user&#96;
+    - Password: &#96;predico_password&#96;
+    - Check &quot;Save password&quot; if you want
+ 5. **Click &quot;Save&quot;**
+ 
+ ### Viewing Database Schema
+ 
+ Once connected, you can:
+ 
+ 1. **Expand the server** → &#96;Databases&#96; → &#96;predico_db&#96; → &#96;Schemas&#96; → &#96;public&#96; → &#96;Tables&#96;
+ 2. **View all tables:**
+    - &#96;users&#96; - User accounts
+    - &#96;teams&#96; - National teams
+    - &#96;games&#96; - World Cup matches
+    - &#96;predictions&#96; - User predictions
+    - &#96;leagues&#96; - Private leagues
+    - &#96;league_members&#96; - League memberships
+    - And more...
+ 
+ 3. **Query the database:**
+    - Right-click on any table → &quot;View/Edit Data&quot; → &quot;All Rows&quot;
+    - Or use the Query Tool to run SQL queries
+ 
+ ### Example Queries
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;sql
+ -- View all users
+ SELECT id, email, username, email_verified, created_at FROM users;
+ 
+ -- View all tables
+ SELECT table_name 
+ FROM information_schema.tables 
+ WHERE table_schema = &#39;public&#39;;
+ 
+ -- Check migration history
+ SELECT * FROM alembic_version;
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Useful Docker Commands
+ 
+ ### Stop Services
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ docker-compose down
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Stop and Remove Volumes (⚠️ This deletes all data!)
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ docker-compose down -v
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Restart a Specific Service
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ docker-compose restart backend
+ docker-compose restart postgres
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Access Container Shell
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Backend container
+ docker-compose exec backend bash
+ 
+ # PostgreSQL container
+ docker-compose exec postgres psql -U predico_user -d predico_db
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Rebuild Containers (after code changes)
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ docker-compose build
+ docker-compose up -d
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Environment Variables
+ 
+ The Docker Compose file uses these default values. You can override them by creating a &#96;.env&#96; file in the project root:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;env
+ # Database
+ POSTGRES_USER=predico_user
+ POSTGRES_PASSWORD=predico_password
+ POSTGRES_DB=predico_db
+ 
+ # Backend
+ SECRET_KEY=dev-secret-key-change-in-production
+ DEBUG=True
+ DATABASE_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://predico_user:predico_password@postgres:5432/predico_db
+ REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379/0
+ 
+ # Frontend
+ VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Troubleshooting
+ 
+ ### Port Already in Use
+ 
+ If you get an error that a port is already in use:
+ 
+ 1. **Check what&#39;s using the port:**
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    # macOS/Linux
+    lsof -i :5432
+    lsof -i :8000
+    lsof -i :3000
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 2. **Change the port in docker-compose.yml:**
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;yaml
+    ports:
+      - &quot;5433:5432&quot;  # Use 5433 instead of 5432
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Database Connection Refused
+ 
+ 1. **Check if PostgreSQL container is running:**
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    docker-compose ps postgres
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 2. **Check PostgreSQL logs:**
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    docker-compose logs postgres
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 3. **Restart the database:**
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    docker-compose restart postgres
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Migration Errors
+ 
+ If migrations fail:
+ 
+ 1. **Check backend logs:**
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    docker-compose logs backend
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 2. **Run migrations manually:**
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    docker-compose exec backend alembic upgrade head
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 3. **If you need to reset the database:**
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    # ⚠️ WARNING: This deletes all data!
+    docker-compose down -v
+    docker-compose up -d
+    docker-compose exec backend alembic upgrade head
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Accessing the Application
+ 
+ Once everything is running:
+ 
+ - **Frontend**: http://localhost:3000
+ - **Backend API**: http://localhost:8000
+ - **API Documentation**: http://localhost:8000/api/docs
+ - **Database**: localhost:5432
+ 
+ ## Next Steps
+ 
+ 1. **Run migrations** (if not done automatically):
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    docker-compose exec backend alembic upgrade head
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 2. **Verify database schema** in pgAdmin
+ 
+ 3. **Test the application**:
+    - Visit http://localhost:3000
+    - Try signing up a new user
+    - Check the &#96;users&#96; table in pgAdmin to see the new user
+ 
+ 4. **Check logs** if something doesn&#39;t work:
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    docker-compose logs -f
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
```

</details>

```diff
+ #!/bin/bash
+ set -e
+ 
+ echo &quot;Waiting for database to be ready...&quot;
+ # Wait for postgres to be ready
+ until pg_isready -h postgres -p 5432 -U predico_user; do
+   echo &quot;PostgreSQL is unavailable - sleeping&quot;
+   sleep 1
+ done
+ 
+ echo &quot;Running database migrations...&quot;
+ alembic upgrade head
+ 
+ echo &quot;Starting application...&quot;
+ exec uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --reload
+ 
```

```diff
- 
+ # Database Migration Guide
+ 
+ This guide explains how to run database migrations for the Predico project.
+ 
+ ## Migration File Created
+ 
+ A migration file has been created at:
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ backend/alembic/versions/001_add_email_verification_fields.py
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ This migration adds the following fields to the &#96;users&#96; table:
+ - &#96;email_verified&#96; (Boolean, default False)
+ - &#96;email_verification_token&#96; (String, nullable, unique, indexed)
+ - &#96;password_reset_token&#96; (String, nullable, unique, indexed)
+ - &#96;password_reset_expires&#96; (DateTime, nullable)
+ 
+ ## Running Migrations
+ 
+ ### Option 1: Using Docker Compose (Recommended)
+ 
+ The docker-compose.yml is configured to automatically run migrations on backend startup:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Start all services (migrations run automatically)
+ docker-compose up -d
+ 
+ # Check backend logs to see migration output
+ docker-compose logs backend
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Option 2: Manual Migration in Docker
+ 
+ If you need to run migrations manually:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Run migrations
+ docker-compose exec backend alembic upgrade head
+ 
+ # Check current migration version
+ docker-compose exec backend alembic current
+ 
+ # View migration history
+ docker-compose exec backend alembic history
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Option 3: Local Development (without Docker)
+ 
+ If running locally without Docker:
+ 
+ 1. **Install dependencies:**
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    cd backend
+    python -m venv venv
+    source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate
+    pip install -r requirements.txt
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 2. **Set up environment variables:**
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    cp .env.example .env
+    # Edit .env with your database URL
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 3. **Run migrations:**
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    alembic upgrade head
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Verifying Migration
+ 
+ ### Using pgAdmin
+ 
+ 1. Connect to the database (see DOCKER_SETUP.md for connection details)
+ 2. Navigate to: &#96;predico_db&#96; → &#96;Schemas&#96; → &#96;public&#96; → &#96;Tables&#96; → &#96;users&#96;
+ 3. Right-click on &#96;users&#96; → &quot;View/Edit Data&quot; → &quot;All Rows&quot;
+ 4. Check the columns - you should see:
+    - &#96;email_verified&#96;
+    - &#96;email_verification_token&#96;
+    - &#96;password_reset_token&#96;
+    - &#96;password_reset_expires&#96;
+ 
+ ### Using SQL Query
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;sql
+ -- Check if columns exist
+ SELECT column_name, data_type, is_nullable, column_default
+ FROM information_schema.columns
+ WHERE table_name = &#39;users&#39;
+ ORDER BY ordinal_position;
+ 
+ -- Check indexes
+ SELECT indexname, indexdef
+ FROM pg_indexes
+ WHERE tablename = &#39;users&#39;;
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Using psql Command Line
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Connect to database
+ docker-compose exec postgres psql -U predico_user -d predico_db
+ 
+ # Check table structure
+ \d users
+ 
+ # Check migration version
+ SELECT * FROM alembic_version;
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Creating New Migrations
+ 
+ When you modify models, create a new migration:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # In Docker
+ docker-compose exec backend alembic revision --autogenerate -m &quot;Description of changes&quot;
+ 
+ # Locally
+ alembic revision --autogenerate -m &quot;Description of changes&quot;
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ Then review the generated migration file in &#96;backend/alembic/versions/&#96; before applying it.
+ 
+ ## Rolling Back Migrations
+ 
+ ⚠️ **Warning**: Only rollback in development. Never rollback in production without backing up data first.
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Rollback one migration
+ docker-compose exec backend alembic downgrade -1
+ 
+ # Rollback to specific revision
+ docker-compose exec backend alembic downgrade &lt;revision_id&gt;
+ 
+ # Rollback all migrations
+ docker-compose exec backend alembic downgrade base
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Troubleshooting
+ 
+ ### Migration Fails
+ 
+ 1. **Check database connection:**
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    docker-compose ps postgres
+    docker-compose logs postgres
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 2. **Check backend logs:**
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    docker-compose logs backend
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 3. **Verify DATABASE_URL:**
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    docker-compose exec backend env | grep DATABASE_URL
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### &quot;Table already exists&quot; Error
+ 
+ If you get errors about tables already existing, the database might have been created manually. You can:
+ 
+ 1. **Mark migration as complete without running it:**
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    docker-compose exec backend alembic stamp head
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 2. **Or reset the database (⚠️ deletes all data):**
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    docker-compose down -v
+    docker-compose up -d
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Migration Out of Sync
+ 
+ If your database schema doesn&#39;t match your models:
+ 
+ 1. **Generate a new migration:**
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    docker-compose exec backend alembic revision --autogenerate -m &quot;Sync schema&quot;
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 2. **Review the migration file carefully**
+ 
+ 3. **Apply it:**
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    docker-compose exec backend alembic upgrade head
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Next Steps
+ 
+ After running migrations:
+ 
+ 1. ✅ Verify the &#96;users&#96; table has the new columns
+ 2. ✅ Test signup functionality
+ 3. ✅ Check that email verification tokens are being stored
+ 4. ✅ Test password reset functionality
+
```

## Summary

### 1. Migration file created
Created migration file: `backend/alembic/versions/001_add_email_verification_fields.py`

This migration adds to the `users` table:
- `email_verified` (Boolean, default False, indexed)
- `email_verification_token` (String, nullable, unique, indexed)
- `password_reset_token` (String, nullable, unique, indexed)
- `password_reset_expires` (DateTime, nullable)

### 2. Docker setup configured
- Updated `docker-compose.yml` to run migrations on backend startup
- Fixed Alembic configuration to use synchronous database URL (psycopg2) for migrations
- Created documentation files

## How to run Docker and check the database

### Step 1: Start all services
```bash
cd /Users/rafael/PycharmProjects/predico
docker-compose up -d
```

This will:
- Start PostgreSQL on port 5432
- Start Redis on port 6379
- Start Backend API on port 8000 (migrations run automatically)
- Start Frontend on port 3000

### Step 2: Verify migrations ran
```bash
# Check backend logs for migration output
docker-compose logs backend | grep -i migration
```

You should see output indicating the migration was applied.

### Step 3: Connect to database with pgAdmin

Connection details:
- Host: `localhost`
- Port: `5432`
- Database: `predico_db`
- Username: `predico_user`
- Password: `predico_password`

Steps in pgAdmin:
1. Right-click "Servers" → "Create" → "Server"
2. General tab: Name it "Predico Local"
3. Connection tab:
   - Host: `localhost`
   - Port: `5432`
   - Database: `predico_db`
   - Username: `predico_user`
   - Password: `predico_password`
4. Click "Save"

### Step 4: Verify the migration

In pgAdmin:
1. Navigate to: `Predico Local` → `Databases` → `predico_db` → `Schemas` → `public` → `Tables` → `users`
2. Right-click `users` → "View/Edit Data" → "All Rows"
3. You should see the new columns:
   - `email_verified`
   - `email_verification_token`
   - `password_reset_token`
   - `password_reset_expires`

Or run this SQL query:
```sql
SELECT column_name, data_type, is_nullable, column_default
FROM information_schema.columns
WHERE table_name = 'users'
ORDER BY ordinal_position;
```

## Documentation created

1. `DOCKER_SETUP.md` — Guide for running Docker and connecting with pgAdmin
2. `MIGRATION_GUIDE.md` — Guide for running and managing migrations

## Quick commands reference

```bash
# Start services
docker-compose up -d

# View logs
docker-compose logs -f backend

# Run migrations manually (if needed)
docker-compose exec backend alembic upgrade head

# Stop services
docker-compose down

# Stop and delete all data (⚠️ careful!)
docker-compose down -v
```

The migration will run automatically when you start the Docker containers. After starting, you can verify the new columns in pgAdmin.

Removed the frontend service from docker-compose.yml and updated the documentation. Changes:

## Changes made

1. Removed frontend service from `docker-compose.yml`
   - Only PostgreSQL, Redis, and Backend services remain
   - Frontend runs separately with `npm run dev`

2. Updated documentation
   - `DOCKER_SETUP.md` — Added instructions for running frontend separately
   - `README.md` — Updated setup instructions

## Updated workflow

### Start backend services (Docker):
```bash
docker-compose up -d
```

This starts:
- PostgreSQL on port 5432
- Redis on port 6379
- Backend API on port 8000

### Start frontend (separate terminal):
```bash
cd frontend
npm install  # First time only
npm run dev
```

Frontend will be available at http://localhost:3000 with hot reloading.

## Benefits

- Faster development — Frontend hot reloads without rebuilding Docker images
- Easier debugging — Direct access to frontend code and dev tools
- Simpler setup — No need to rebuild frontend container on code changes
- Better performance — Vite dev server runs natively

The backend CORS is already configured to allow requests from `http://localhost:3000`, so the frontend can communicate with the backend API without issues.

You can now run `docker-compose up -d` to start the backend services, and then run `npm run dev` in the frontend directory to start the development server.

## pgAdmin Connection Parameters

**General Tab:**
- **Name**: `Predico Local` (or any name you prefer)

**Connection Tab:**
- **Host name/address**: `localhost` (or `127.0.0.1`)
- **Port**: `5432`
- **Maintenance database**: `predico_db`
- **Username**: `predico_user`
- **Password**: `predico_password`
- **Save password**: ✓ (optional, but recommended)

**Advanced Tab (optional):**
- Leave defaults

**SSL Tab (optional):**
- SSL mode: `Prefer` or `Disable` (for local development)

## Quick Steps in pgAdmin

1. Right-click "Servers" in the left panel
2. Select "Create" → "Server"
3. Fill in the General tab (name)
4. Fill in the Connection tab with the values above
5. Click "Save"

After connecting, navigate to:
- `Predico Local` → `Databases` → `predico_db` → `Schemas` → `public` → `Tables`

You should see tables like `users`, `teams`, `games`, `predictions`, etc.

Note: Make sure Docker Compose is running (`docker-compose up -d`) before connecting, otherwise PostgreSQL won't be available.

Fixed the permission issue. The problem was that packages were installed in `/root/.local/bin`, but the container runs as `appuser` (non-root) and couldn't access them.

## What I Fixed

1. Updated the Dockerfile to copy packages to `/home/appuser/.local` (accessible by the appuser)
2. Set proper ownership so appuser can access the files
3. Updated PATH to include `/home/appuser/.local/bin`

## Rebuild and Restart

Rebuild the backend container to apply the changes:

```bash
# Stop the containers
docker-compose down

# Rebuild the backend image
docker-compose build backend

# Start everything again
docker-compose up -d

# Check the logs to verify it's working
docker-compose logs -f backend
```

You should see the migration running successfully and the backend starting without permission errors.

If you still see issues, you can also try:

```bash
# Force rebuild without cache
docker-compose build --no-cache backend
docker-compose up -d
```

The `alembic` command should now work because it's in a location accessible by the `appuser`.

Rebuild the backend image since the Dockerfile changed. Steps:

## Recommended approach

**Step 1: Stop the containers**
```bash
docker-compose down
```
Or if you're using newer Docker:
```bash
docker compose down
```

**Step 2: Rebuild the backend image**
```bash
docker-compose build backend
```
Or:
```bash
docker compose build backend
```

**Step 3: Start everything again**
```bash
docker-compose up -d
```
Or:
```bash
docker compose up -d
```

**Step 4: Verify it's working**
```bash
docker-compose logs -f backend
```

## Alternative: one-liner

You can also do it all at once:
```bash
docker-compose down && docker-compose build backend && docker-compose up -d
```

## Why this approach

- `docker-compose down` stops and removes containers (keeps volumes)
- `docker-compose build backend` rebuilds only the backend image with the new Dockerfile
- `docker-compose up -d` starts everything fresh

You don't need to tear down volumes (`-v` flag) unless you want to reset the database. The current approach preserves your database data.

After running these commands, check the logs to confirm the migration runs and the backend starts successfully.

**Step 1: Stop the containers**
```bash
docker compose down
```

**Step 2: Rebuild the backend image**
```bash
docker compose build backend
```

**Step 3: Start everything again**
```bash
docker compose up -d
```

**Step 4: Verify it's working**
```bash
docker compose logs -f backend
```

## One-liner
```bash
docker compose down && docker compose build backend && docker compose up -d
```

I'll use `docker compose` (with a space) in all future commands. This is the modern Docker Compose V2 syntax that's integrated into the Docker CLI.

Fixed the issue: Alembic was using async migrations with `psycopg2` (sync driver). Converted it to synchronous migrations, which is standard for Alembic.

## What I Changed

1. Removed async imports — replaced `async_engine_from_config` with `engine_from_config`
2. Converted to synchronous migrations — `run_migrations_online()` is now a regular function, not async
3. Simplified the migration flow — uses standard synchronous SQLAlchemy engine

## Next Steps

Restart the backend container to apply the changes:

```bash
# Restart the backend (no need to rebuild since we only changed Python code)
docker compose restart backend

# Or if that doesn't work, rebuild:
docker compose down
docker compose build backend
docker compose up -d

# Check the logs
docker compose logs -f backend
```

The migrations should now run successfully. Alembic will use `psycopg2` synchronously, which is the standard approach for database migrations.

The application code still uses `asyncpg` for async operations, but migrations run synchronously, which is the recommended pattern.

```diff
+
```

```diff
+ ## Option 3: Use Alembic Stamp
+
```

## Quick Fix (Recommended for Development)

Since you're in development and likely don't have important data yet:

```bash
# Stop and remove everything (including database data)
docker compose down -v

# Rebuild and start fresh
docker compose build backend
docker compose up -d

# Check logs
docker compose logs -f backend
```

## Alternative: Keep Data and Fix Manually

If you want to keep existing data:

```bash
# Connect to database and clear the alembic_version table
docker compose exec postgres psql -U predico_user -d predico_db -c "DELETE FROM alembic_version;"

# Restart backend (it will run migrations from scratch)
docker compose restart backend

# Check logs
docker compose logs -f backend
```

The first option (down -v) is simplest for development. It resets everything and runs the migrations with the new shorter revision IDs.

```diff
@@ -1,1 +1,248 @@
- 
+ # AWS Multi-Environment Setup Guide
+ 
+ This guide walks you through setting up a complete CI/CD pipeline with multiple environments (local → dev → staging → production) in AWS.
+ 
+ ## Architecture Overview
+ 
+ ### Services We&#39;re Using
+ 
+ 1. **ECS Fargate** - Serverless containers for backend (no EC2 to manage)
+ 2. **RDS PostgreSQL** - Managed database service
+ 3. **ElastiCache Redis** - Managed Redis for caching
+ 4. **Application Load Balancer (ALB)** - Routes traffic to ECS tasks
+ 5. **ECR** - Container registry for Docker images
+ 6. **S3 + CloudFront** - Static assets and CDN
+ 7. **Secrets Manager** - Secure storage for passwords and API keys
+ 8. **GitHub Actions** - CI/CD pipeline (or AWS CodePipeline)
+ 
+ ### Why This Architecture?
+ 
+ - **Serverless Containers (Fargate)**: No EC2 instances to manage, auto-scales, pay only for what you use
+ - **Managed Database (RDS)**: Automatic backups, high availability, easy scaling
+ - **Multi-Environment**: Separate infrastructure for dev/staging/prod with proper isolation
+ 
+ ## Step-by-Step Setup
+ 
+ ### Phase 1: Initial AWS Setup (One-Time)
+ 
+ #### Step 1.1: Create IAM User for Terraform
+ 
+ **Why**: Never use root account credentials. Create a dedicated IAM user with limited permissions.
+ 
+ 1. Go to AWS Console → IAM → Users → &quot;Add users&quot;
+ 2. Username: &#96;predico-terraform&#96;
+ 3. Access type: &quot;Programmatic access&quot; (for API/CLI)
+ 4. Permissions: Attach policy &#96;AdministratorAccess&#96; (or create custom policy - see below)
+ 5. **Save the Access Key ID and Secret Access Key** - you&#39;ll need these!
+ 
+ **Custom IAM Policy** (more secure, recommended):
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;json
+ {
+   &quot;Version&quot;: &quot;2012-10-17&quot;,
+   &quot;Statement&quot;: [
+     {
+       &quot;Effect&quot;: &quot;Allow&quot;,
+       &quot;Action&quot;: &quot;*&quot;,
+       &quot;Resource&quot;: &quot;*&quot;,
+       &quot;Condition&quot;: {
+         &quot;StringEquals&quot;: {
+           &quot;aws:RequestTag/ManagedBy&quot;: &quot;terraform&quot;
+         }
+       }
+     }
+   ]
+ }
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ #### Step 1.2: Configure AWS CLI
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Install AWS CLI if not already installed
+ # macOS: brew install awscli
+ # Or download from: https://aws.amazon.com/cli/
+ 
+ # Configure with your IAM user credentials
+ aws configure
+ 
+ # Enter:
+ # AWS Access Key ID: [from Step 1.1]
+ # AWS Secret Access Key: [from Step 1.1]
+ # Default region: us-east-1
+ # Default output format: json
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ #### Step 1.3: Create S3 Bucket for Terraform State
+ 
+ **Why**: Store Terraform state remotely so multiple people/environments can work together.
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Create bucket for Terraform state (must be globally unique)
+ aws s3 mb s3://predico-terraform-state-$(whoami) --region us-east-1
+ 
+ # Enable versioning (important for state files)
+ aws s3api put-bucket-versioning \
+   --bucket predico-terraform-state-$(whoami) \
+   --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled
+ 
+ # Enable encryption
+ aws s3api put-bucket-encryption \
+   --bucket predico-terraform-state-$(whoami) \
+   --server-side-encryption-configuration &#39;{
+     &quot;Rules&quot;: [{
+       &quot;ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault&quot;: {
+         &quot;SSEAlgorithm&quot;: &quot;AES256&quot;
+       }
+     }]
+   }&#39;
+ 
+ # Create DynamoDB table for state locking (prevents concurrent modifications)
+ aws dynamodb create-table \
+   --table-name predico-terraform-locks \
+   --attribute-definitions AttributeName=LockID,AttributeType=S \
+   --key-schema AttributeName=LockID,KeyType=HASH \
+   --billing-mode PAY_PER_REQUEST \
+   --region us-east-1
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ **Note**: Replace &#96;$(whoami)&#96; with your username or a unique identifier.
+ 
+ ### Phase 2: Terraform Multi-Environment Setup
+ 
+ #### Step 2.1: Restructure Terraform for Multiple Environments
+ 
+ We&#39;ll use Terraform workspaces to manage multiple environments.
+ 
+ #### Step 2.2: Update Terraform Backend Configuration
+ 
+ Update &#96;infrastructure/terraform/main.tf&#96; to use remote state (we&#39;ll do this in code).
+ 
+ ### Phase 3: Deploy Dev Environment (First)
+ 
+ #### Step 3.1: Configure Dev Environment
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ cd infrastructure/terraform
+ 
+ # Create dev workspace
+ terraform workspace new dev
+ 
+ # Or select existing
+ terraform workspace select dev
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ #### Step 3.2: Create Dev Variables File
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ cp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars.dev
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ Edit &#96;terraform.tfvars.dev&#96;:
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;hcl
+ aws_region            = &quot;us-east-1&quot;
+ environment           = &quot;dev&quot;
+ project_name          = &quot;predico&quot;
+ db_instance_class     = &quot;db.t3.micro&quot;  # Small for dev
+ db_allocated_storage  = 20
+ db_max_allocated_storage = 100
+ fargate_cpu           = 256  # Smaller for dev
+ fargate_memory        = 512
+ min_capacity          = 1
+ max_capacity          = 3
+ domain_name           = &quot;&quot;  # No domain for dev
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ #### Step 3.3: Initialize and Deploy Dev
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ terraform init
+ 
+ # Review what will be created
+ terraform plan -var-file=terraform.tfvars.dev
+ 
+ # Apply (creates all infrastructure)
+ terraform apply -var-file=terraform.tfvars.dev
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ This will take 15-20 minutes to create all resources.
+ 
+ ### Phase 4: Set Up CI/CD Pipeline
+ 
+ We&#39;ll use GitHub Actions for CI/CD.
+ 
+ #### Step 4.1: Create GitHub Secrets
+ 
+ In your GitHub repository → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions:
+ 
+ Add these secrets:
+ - &#96;AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID&#96; - Your IAM user access key
+ - &#96;AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY&#96; - Your IAM user secret key
+ - &#96;AWS_REGION&#96; - &#96;us-east-1&#96;
+ 
+ #### Step 4.2: Create GitHub Actions Workflow
+ 
+ We&#39;ll create workflow files that:
+ - Run tests on every push
+ - Deploy to dev on merge to &#96;develop&#96; branch
+ - Deploy to staging on merge to &#96;staging&#96; branch
+ - Deploy to production on merge to &#96;main&#96; branch (with manual approval)
+ 
+ ### Phase 5: Deploy Staging and Production
+ 
+ Repeat Phase 3 with different variable files for staging and production.
+ 
+ ## Environment-Specific Configurations
+ 
+ ### Dev Environment
+ - Small instance sizes
+ - Single AZ (cheaper)
+ - No domain required
+ - Auto-scaling: 1-3 tasks
+ - RDS: db.t3.micro
+ 
+ ### Staging Environment
+ - Medium instance sizes
+ - Multi-AZ for high availability
+ - Optional domain
+ - Auto-scaling: 2-5 tasks
+ - RDS: db.t3.small
+ 
+ ### Production Environment
+ - Larger instance sizes
+ - Multi-AZ required
+ - Custom domain required
+ - Auto-scaling: 3-20 tasks
+ - RDS: db.t3.medium or larger
+ - Enhanced monitoring
+ - Backup retention: 30 days
+ 
+ ## Cost Estimates (Monthly)
+ 
+ ### Dev Environment
+ - ECS Fargate: ~$15-30
+ - RDS: ~$15-20
+ - ALB: ~$16
+ - ElastiCache: ~$10-15
+ - S3/CloudFront: ~$5
+ - **Total: ~$60-85/month**
+ 
+ ### Staging Environment
+ - Similar to dev: ~$60-85/month
+ 
+ ### Production Environment
+ - ECS Fargate: ~$50-200 (depends on traffic)
+ - RDS: ~$50-150
+ - ALB: ~$16
+ - ElastiCache: ~$30-50
+ - S3/CloudFront: ~$10-50
+ - **Total: ~$150-500/month** (scales with usage)
+ 
+ ## Next Steps
+ 
+ 1. Follow Phase 1 (Initial AWS Setup)
+ 2. We&#39;ll restructure Terraform for multi-environment
+ 3. Deploy dev environment
+ 4. Set up CI/CD pipeline
+ 5. Deploy staging and production
+ 
+ Let me know when you&#39;ve completed Phase 1, and we&#39;ll proceed to the next steps!
+ 
```

```diff
@@ -1,1 +1,59 @@
- 
+ # Environment-Specific Terraform Configuration
+ 
+ This directory contains environment-specific configurations for dev, staging, and production.
+ 
+ ## Structure
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ envs/
+ ├── dev/
+ │   ├── backend.hcl          # Terraform state backend config
+ │   └── terraform.tfvars     # Environment variables
+ ├── staging/
+ │   ├── backend.hcl
+ │   └── terraform.tfvars
+ └── production/
+     ├── backend.hcl
+     └── terraform.tfvars
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Usage
+ 
+ ### Initialize for an Environment
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # From infrastructure/terraform directory
+ cd ../..  # Go to project root
+ cd infrastructure/terraform
+ 
+ # Initialize with dev backend
+ terraform init -backend-config=envs/dev/backend.hcl
+ 
+ # Plan with dev variables
+ terraform plan -var-file=envs/dev/terraform.tfvars
+ 
+ # Apply
+ terraform apply -var-file=envs/dev/terraform.tfvars
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Switch Environments
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # For staging
+ terraform init -reconfigure -backend-config=envs/staging/backend.hcl
+ terraform plan -var-file=envs/staging/terraform.tfvars
+ terraform apply -var-file=envs/staging/terraform.tfvars
+ 
+ # For production
+ terraform init -reconfigure -backend-config=envs/production/backend.hcl
+ terraform plan -var-file=envs/production/terraform.tfvars
+ terraform apply -var-file=envs/production/terraform.tfvars
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Important Notes
+ 
+ 1. **Never commit sensitive data** - Use AWS Secrets Manager for passwords and API keys
+ 2. **Always review plan** before applying, especially for production
+ 3. **Use separate AWS accounts** for production if possible (best practice)
+ 4. **Backup before major changes** in production
+ 
```

</details>

</tool-use>

```diff
+ name: CI/CD Pipeline
+

+           --health-retries 5
+         ports:

+       
+       redis:
+         image: redis:7

+           REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379/0

+         run: |

+       - name: Set up Node.js

+         working-directory: ./frontend

+       - name: Lint frontend

+     needs: test

+           aws-secret-access-key: ${{ secrets.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}

+       - name: Login to Amazon ECR

+       - name: Determine environment

+           if [[ &quot;${{ github.ref }}&quot; == &quot;refs/heads/main&quot; ]]; then

+           elif [[ &quot;${{ github.ref }}&quot; == &quot;refs/heads/staging&quot; ]]; then
+             echo &quot;environment=staging&quot; &gt;&gt; $GITHUB_OUTPUT
+           else
+             echo &quot;environment=dev&quot; &gt;&gt; $GITHUB_OUTPUT
+           fi
+       
+       - name: Build, tag, and push backend image
+         env:

+           IMAGE_TAG: ${{ steps.env.outputs.environment }}-${{ github.sha }}

+           docker push $ECR_REGISTRY/$ECR_REPOSITORY:latest
```

```diff
- 
+ #!/bin/bash
+ # AWS Initial Setup Script
+ # This script helps set up the initial AWS resources needed for Terraform
+ 
+ set -e
+ 
+ echo &quot;🚀 Predico AWS Setup Script&quot;
+ echo &quot;============================&quot;
+ echo &quot;&quot;
+ 
+ # Colors for output
+ RED=&#39;\033[0;31m&#39;
+ GREEN=&#39;\033[0;32m&#39;
+ YELLOW=&#39;\033[1;33m&#39;
+ NC=&#39;\033[0m&#39; # No Color
+ 
+ # Check if AWS CLI is installed
+ if ! command -v aws &amp;&gt; /dev/null; then
+     echo -e &quot;${RED}❌ AWS CLI is not installed.${NC}&quot;
+     echo &quot;Please install it from: https://aws.amazon.com/cli/&quot;
+     exit 1
+ fi
+ 
+ # Check if AWS credentials are configured
+ if ! aws sts get-caller-identity &amp;&gt; /dev/null; then
+     echo -e &quot;${RED}❌ AWS credentials not configured.${NC}&quot;
+     echo &quot;Please run: aws configure&quot;
+     exit 1
+ fi
+ 
+ echo -e &quot;${GREEN}✅ AWS CLI is installed and configured${NC}&quot;
+ echo &quot;&quot;
+ 
+ # Get AWS account ID
+ AWS_ACCOUNT_ID=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text)
+ AWS_REGION=${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}
+ BUCKET_NAME=&quot;predico-terraform-state-${AWS_ACCOUNT_ID}&quot;
+ 
+ echo &quot;AWS Account ID: ${AWS_ACCOUNT_ID}&quot;
+ echo &quot;AWS Region: ${AWS_REGION}&quot;
+ echo &quot;State Bucket: ${BUCKET_NAME}&quot;
+ echo &quot;&quot;
+ 
+ read -p &quot;Continue with setup? (y/n) &quot; -n 1 -r
+ echo
+ if [[ ! $REPLY =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]; then
+     exit 1
+ fi
+ 
+ # Step 1: Create S3 bucket for Terraform state
+ echo &quot;&quot;
+ echo &quot;📦 Step 1: Creating S3 bucket for Terraform state...&quot;
+ if aws s3 ls &quot;s3://${BUCKET_NAME}&quot; 2&gt;&amp;1 | grep -q &#39;NoSuchBucket&#39;; then
+     aws s3 mb &quot;s3://${BUCKET_NAME}&quot; --region &quot;${AWS_REGION}&quot;
+     echo -e &quot;${GREEN}✅ Created S3 bucket: ${BUCKET_NAME}${NC}&quot;
+ else
+     echo -e &quot;${YELLOW}⚠️  Bucket ${BUCKET_NAME} already exists${NC}&quot;
+ fi
+ 
+ # Enable versioning
+ echo &quot;Enabling versioning...&quot;
+ aws s3api put-bucket-versioning \
+     --bucket &quot;${BUCKET_NAME}&quot; \
+     --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled \
+     --region &quot;${AWS_REGION}&quot; 2&gt;/dev/null || echo -e &quot;${YELLOW}⚠️  Versioning already enabled${NC}&quot;
+ 
+ # Enable encryption
+ echo &quot;Enabling encryption...&quot;
+ aws s3api put-bucket-encryption \
+     --bucket &quot;${BUCKET_NAME}&quot; \
+     --server-side-encryption-configuration &#39;{
+         &quot;Rules&quot;: [{
+             &quot;ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault&quot;: {
+                 &quot;SSEAlgorithm&quot;: &quot;AES256&quot;
+             }
+         }]
+     }&#39; \
+     --region &quot;${AWS_REGION}&quot; 2&gt;/dev/null || echo -e &quot;${YELLOW}⚠️  Encryption already enabled${NC}&quot;
+ 
+ # Block public access
+ echo &quot;Blocking public access...&quot;
+ aws s3api put-public-access-block \
+     --bucket &quot;${BUCKET_NAME}&quot; \
+     --public-access-block-configuration \
+     &quot;BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true&quot; \
+     --region &quot;${AWS_REGION}&quot; 2&gt;/dev/null || echo -e &quot;${YELLOW}⚠️  Public access already blocked${NC}&quot;
+ 
+ # Step 2: Create DynamoDB table for state locking
+ echo &quot;&quot;
+ echo &quot;🔒 Step 2: Creating DynamoDB table for state locking...&quot;
+ TABLE_NAME=&quot;predico-terraform-locks&quot;
+ if aws dynamodb describe-table --table-name &quot;${TABLE_NAME}&quot; --region &quot;${AWS_REGION}&quot; &amp;&gt;/dev/null; then
+     echo -e &quot;${YELLOW}⚠️  Table ${TABLE_NAME} already exists${NC}&quot;
+ else
+     aws dynamodb create-table \
+         --table-name &quot;${TABLE_NAME}&quot; \
+         --attribute-definitions AttributeName=LockID,AttributeType=S \
+         --key-schema AttributeName=LockID,KeyType=HASH \
+         --billing-mode PAY_PER_REQUEST \
+         --region &quot;${AWS_REGION}&quot;
+     
+     echo &quot;Waiting for table to be active...&quot;
+     aws dynamodb wait table-exists --table-name &quot;${TABLE_NAME}&quot; --region &quot;${AWS_REGION}&quot;
+     echo -e &quot;${GREEN}✅ Created DynamoDB table: ${TABLE_NAME}${NC}&quot;
+ fi
+ 
+ # Step 3: Update backend configuration files
+ echo &quot;&quot;
+ echo &quot;📝 Step 3: Updating backend configuration files...&quot;
+ for env in dev staging production; do
+     BACKEND_FILE=&quot;terraform/envs/${env}/backend.hcl&quot;
+     if [ -f &quot;${BACKEND_FILE}&quot; ]; then
+         # Update bucket name in backend files
+         sed -i.bak &quot;s/bucket.*=.*predico-terraform-state/bucket = \&quot;${BUCKET_NAME}\&quot;/&quot; &quot;${BACKEND_FILE}&quot;
+         rm -f &quot;${BACKEND_FILE}.bak&quot;
+         echo -e &quot;${GREEN}✅ Updated ${BACKEND_FILE}${NC}&quot;
+     fi
+ done
+ 
+ echo &quot;&quot;
+ echo -e &quot;${GREEN}🎉 Setup complete!${NC}&quot;
+ echo &quot;&quot;
+ echo &quot;Next steps:&quot;
+ echo &quot;1. Review and update backend.hcl files if needed&quot;
+ echo &quot;2. Run: cd infrastructure/terraform&quot;
+ echo &quot;3. Initialize Terraform: terraform init -backend-config=envs/dev/backend.hcl&quot;
+ echo &quot;4. Plan: terraform plan -var-file=envs/dev/terraform.tfvars&quot;
+ echo &quot;5. Apply: terraform apply -var-file=envs/dev/terraform.tfvars&quot;
+ echo &quot;&quot;
+ echo &quot;Your AWS Account ID: ${AWS_ACCOUNT_ID}&quot;
+ echo &quot;Add this to GitHub Secrets as AWS_ACCOUNT_ID&quot;
+ 
```

</details>

</tool-use>

```diff
@@ -1,1 +1,365 @@
- 
+ # Step-by-Step AWS Multi-Environment Setup
+ 
+ This is your complete guide to set up the Predico project in AWS with dev, staging, and production environments.
+ 
+ ## Architecture Overview
+ 
+ **We&#39;re using:**
+ - ✅ **ECS Fargate** (Serverless containers) - Hosts your backend API
+ - ✅ **RDS PostgreSQL** (Managed database) - Your database
+ - ✅ **ElastiCache Redis** - Caching layer
+ - ✅ **Application Load Balancer** - Routes traffic
+ - ✅ **ECR** - Stores Docker images
+ - ✅ **S3 + CloudFront** - Static assets
+ - ✅ **GitHub Actions** - CI/CD pipeline
+ 
+ **This is NOT fully serverless** (like Lambda), but uses **serverless containers** (Fargate) which means:
+ - No EC2 instances to manage
+ - Auto-scales based on demand
+ - Pay only for what you use
+ - Still runs Docker containers
+ 
+ ## Phase 1: Initial AWS Setup (Do This First)
+ 
+ ### Step 1.1: Create IAM User for Terraform
+ 
+ **⚠️ IMPORTANT: Never use root account credentials for Terraform!**
+ 
+ 1. Go to [AWS Console](https://console.aws.amazon.com)
+ 2. Navigate to **IAM** → **Users** → **Add users**
+ 3. Username: &#96;predico-terraform&#96;
+ 4. Access type: Select **&quot;Access key - Programmatic access&quot;**
+ 5. Permissions: Click **&quot;Attach policies directly&quot;** → Search and select **&quot;AdministratorAccess&quot;**
+    - (For production, create a custom policy with limited permissions - see AWS_SETUP_GUIDE.md)
+ 6. Click **&quot;Next&quot;** → **&quot;Create user&quot;**
+ 7. **⚠️ CRITICAL: Save these credentials immediately!**
+    - Access Key ID: &#96;AKIA...&#96;
+    - Secret Access Key: &#96;...&#96; (only shown once!)
+ 
+ ### Step 1.2: Configure AWS CLI
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Install AWS CLI if needed
+ # macOS: brew install awscli
+ # Or download: https://aws.amazon.com/cli/
+ 
+ # Configure with your IAM user credentials
+ aws configure
+ 
+ # Enter:
+ # AWS Access Key ID: [paste from Step 1.1]
+ # AWS Secret Access Key: [paste from Step 1.1]
+ # Default region name: us-east-1
+ # Default output format: json
+ 
+ # Verify it works
+ aws sts get-caller-identity
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ You should see your account ID and user ARN.
+ 
+ ### Step 1.3: Run Setup Script
+ 
+ We&#39;ve created a script to set up the initial AWS resources:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ cd infrastructure/scripts
+ ./setup-aws.sh
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ This script will:
+ - Create S3 bucket for Terraform state
+ - Enable versioning and encryption
+ - Create DynamoDB table for state locking
+ - Update backend configuration files
+ 
+ **Or manually** (if script doesn&#39;t work):
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Get your AWS account ID
+ AWS_ACCOUNT_ID=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text)
+ BUCKET_NAME=&quot;predico-terraform-state-${AWS_ACCOUNT_ID}&quot;
+ 
+ # Create S3 bucket
+ aws s3 mb s3://${BUCKET_NAME} --region us-east-1
+ 
+ # Enable versioning
+ aws s3api put-bucket-versioning \
+   --bucket ${BUCKET_NAME} \
+   --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled
+ 
+ # Enable encryption
+ aws s3api put-bucket-encryption \
+   --bucket ${BUCKET_NAME} \
+   --server-side-encryption-configuration &#39;{
+     &quot;Rules&quot;: [{
+       &quot;ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault&quot;: {
+         &quot;SSEAlgorithm&quot;: &quot;AES256&quot;
+       }
+     }]
+   }&#39;
+ 
+ # Create DynamoDB table for locking
+ aws dynamodb create-table \
+   --table-name predico-terraform-locks \
+   --attribute-definitions AttributeName=LockID,AttributeType=S \
+   --key-schema AttributeName=LockID,KeyType=HASH \
+   --billing-mode PAY_PER_REQUEST \
+   --region us-east-1
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Step 1.4: Update Backend Configuration
+ 
+ After running the script, update the backend.hcl files with your bucket name:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Get your account ID
+ AWS_ACCOUNT_ID=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text)
+ 
+ # Update all backend files
+ find infrastructure/terraform/envs -name &quot;backend.hcl&quot; -exec sed -i &#39;&#39; &quot;s/predico-terraform-state/predico-terraform-state-${AWS_ACCOUNT_ID}/g&quot; {} \;
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Phase 2: Deploy Dev Environment
+ 
+ ### Step 2.1: Initialize Terraform for Dev
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ cd infrastructure/terraform
+ 
+ # Initialize with dev backend configuration
+ terraform init -backend-config=envs/dev/backend.hcl
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Step 2.2: Review What Will Be Created
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Plan the deployment
+ terraform plan -var-file=envs/dev/terraform.tfvars
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ Review the output carefully. It will show all resources that will be created.
+ 
+ ### Step 2.3: Deploy Dev Environment
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Apply the configuration (creates all resources)
+ terraform apply -var-file=envs/dev/terraform.tfvars
+ 
+ # Type &quot;yes&quot; when prompted
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ **⏱️ This will take 15-20 minutes** to create all resources.
+ 
+ ### Step 2.4: Save Important Outputs
+ 
+ After deployment completes:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Get important values
+ terraform output
+ 
+ # Save these for later:
+ # - ecr_backend_repository_url
+ # - ecr_frontend_repository_url
+ # - alb_dns_name
+ # - rds_endpoint
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Phase 3: Set Up GitHub Actions CI/CD
+ 
+ ### Step 3.1: Add GitHub Secrets
+ 
+ Go to your GitHub repository:
+ 1. **Settings** → **Secrets and variables** → **Actions**
+ 2. Click **&quot;New repository secret&quot;**
+ 3. Add these secrets:
+ 
+    - **Name**: &#96;AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID&#96;
+      **Value**: Your IAM user access key from Step 1.1
+ 
+    - **Name**: &#96;AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY&#96;
+      **Value**: Your IAM user secret key from Step 1.1
+ 
+    - **Name**: &#96;AWS_ACCOUNT_ID&#96;
+      **Value**: Your AWS account ID (get it with &#96;aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text&#96;)
+ 
+ ### Step 3.2: Create Branch Structure
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Create branches for different environments
+ git checkout -b develop
+ git push -u origin develop
+ 
+ git checkout -b staging
+ git push -u origin staging
+ 
+ # Main branch is already production
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Step 3.3: Test CI/CD
+ 
+ The GitHub Actions workflow will:
+ - **On push to &#96;develop&#96;**: Deploy to dev environment
+ - **On push to &#96;staging&#96;**: Deploy to staging environment  
+ - **On push to &#96;main&#96;**: Deploy to production (requires approval)
+ 
+ Push a change to test:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ git checkout develop
+ # Make a small change
+ git add .
+ git commit -m &quot;test: CI/CD pipeline&quot;
+ git push
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ Check GitHub Actions tab to see the pipeline run.
+ 
+ ## Phase 4: Deploy Staging Environment
+ 
+ ### Step 4.1: Initialize Terraform for Staging
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ cd infrastructure/terraform
+ 
+ # Reinitialize with staging backend
+ terraform init -reconfigure -backend-config=envs/staging/backend.hcl
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Step 4.2: Deploy Staging
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ terraform plan -var-file=envs/staging/terraform.tfvars
+ terraform apply -var-file=envs/staging/terraform.tfvars
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Phase 5: Deploy Production Environment
+ 
+ ### Step 5.1: Get a Domain (Optional but Recommended)
+ 
+ 1. Register a domain (Route 53, Namecheap, etc.)
+ 2. Update &#96;envs/production/terraform.tfvars&#96;:
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;hcl
+    domain_name = &quot;yourdomain.com&quot;
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Step 5.2: Initialize Terraform for Production
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ cd infrastructure/terraform
+ 
+ # Reinitialize with production backend
+ terraform init -reconfigure -backend-config=envs/production/backend.hcl
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Step 5.3: Deploy Production
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Review carefully!
+ terraform plan -var-file=envs/production/terraform.tfvars
+ 
+ # Apply (be careful - this is production!)
+ terraform apply -var-file=envs/production/terraform.tfvars
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Phase 6: Configure GitHub Environments
+ 
+ For production deployments to require approval:
+ 
+ 1. Go to GitHub repository → **Settings** → **Environments**
+ 2. Click **&quot;New environment&quot;**
+ 3. Name: &#96;production&#96;
+ 4. Enable **&quot;Required reviewers&quot;** (add yourself)
+ 5. Save
+ 
+ Now production deployments will require manual approval in GitHub Actions.
+ 
+ ## Quick Reference Commands
+ 
+ ### Switch Between Environments
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ cd infrastructure/terraform
+ 
+ # Dev
+ terraform init -reconfigure -backend-config=envs/dev/backend.hcl
+ terraform plan -var-file=envs/dev/terraform.tfvars
+ 
+ # Staging
+ terraform init -reconfigure -backend-config=envs/staging/backend.hcl
+ terraform plan -var-file=envs/staging/terraform.tfvars
+ 
+ # Production
+ terraform init -reconfigure -backend-config=envs/production/backend.hcl
+ terraform plan -var-file=envs/production/terraform.tfvars
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### View Resources
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # List all resources
+ terraform state list
+ 
+ # Show specific resource
+ terraform state show aws_ecs_cluster.main
+ 
+ # Get outputs
+ terraform output
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Destroy Environment (⚠️ Careful!)
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Only for dev/staging - NEVER for production without backup!
+ terraform destroy -var-file=envs/dev/terraform.tfvars
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Troubleshooting
+ 
+ ### &quot;Bucket already exists&quot;
+ - S3 bucket names are globally unique
+ - Use a different name or add your account ID
+ 
+ ### &quot;Access Denied&quot;
+ - Check IAM user has correct permissions
+ - Verify AWS credentials: &#96;aws sts get-caller-identity&#96;
+ 
+ ### &quot;State locked&quot;
+ - Another Terraform operation is running
+ - Or previous operation crashed
+ - Check DynamoDB table: &#96;aws dynamodb scan --table-name predico-terraform-locks&#96;
+ 
+ ### Terraform state out of sync
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Refresh state
+ terraform refresh -var-file=envs/dev/terraform.tfvars
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Cost Monitoring
+ 
+ Set up billing alerts:
+ 
+ 1. AWS Console → **Billing** → **Billing preferences**
+ 2. Enable **&quot;Receive Billing Alerts&quot;**
+ 3. **CloudWatch** → **Alarms** → **Create alarm**
+ 4. Metric: &#96;EstimatedCharges&#96;
+ 5. Threshold: Set your budget limit
+ 
+ ## Next Steps After Setup
+ 
+ 1. ✅ Configure domain and SSL certificates
+ 2. ✅ Set up monitoring and alerts
+ 3. ✅ Configure backup schedules
+ 4. ✅ Set up log aggregation
+ 5. ✅ Configure auto-scaling policies
+ 6. ✅ Set up database read replicas (for production)
+ 
+ ## Support
+ 
+ If you get stuck:
+ 1. Check AWS CloudWatch logs
+ 2. Check Terraform state: &#96;terraform show&#96;
+ 3. Review AWS Console for resource status
+ 4. Check GitHub Actions logs for CI/CD issues
+ 
```

```diff
+ # Quick Start: AWS Multi-Environment Setup
+ 
+ ## TL;DR - Get Started in 5 Steps
+ 
+ ### 1. Create IAM User (5 minutes)
+ - AWS Console → IAM → Users → Add user
+ - Name: &#96;predico-terraform&#96;
+ - Access: Programmatic access
+ - Permissions: AdministratorAccess
+ - **Save the credentials!**
+ 
+ ### 2. Configure AWS CLI (1 minute)
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ aws configure
+ # Enter your IAM user credentials
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### 3. Run Setup Script (2 minutes)
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ cd infrastructure/scripts
+ ./setup-aws.sh
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### 4. Deploy Dev Environment (20 minutes)
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ cd infrastructure/terraform
+ terraform init -backend-config=envs/dev/backend.hcl
+ terraform plan -var-file=envs/dev/terraform.tfvars
+ terraform apply -var-file=envs/dev/terraform.tfvars
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### 5. Set Up GitHub Actions (5 minutes)
+ - Add secrets to GitHub: &#96;AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID&#96;, &#96;AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY&#96;, &#96;AWS_ACCOUNT_ID&#96;
+ - Push to &#96;develop&#96; branch to trigger dev deployment
+ 
+ ## Architecture Summary
+ 
+ **Backend Hosting**: ECS Fargate (Serverless containers)
+ - No EC2 to manage
+ - Auto-scales automatically
+ - Pay per use
+ 
+ **Database**: RDS PostgreSQL (Managed)
+ - Automatic backups
+ - High availability
+ - Easy scaling
+ 
+ **Environments**:
+ - **Local**: Docker Compose (your machine)
+ - **Dev**: Small instances, single AZ
+ - **Staging**: Medium instances, multi-AZ
+ - **Production**: Large instances, multi-AZ, custom domain
+ 
+ ## Detailed Guides
+ 
+ - **Complete Step-by-Step**: See &#96;STEP_BY_STEP_SETUP.md&#96;
+ - **Architecture Details**: See &#96;AWS_SETUP_GUIDE.md&#96;
+ - **Deployment**: See &#96;DEPLOYMENT.md&#96;
+ 
+ ## Cost Estimates
+ 
+ - **Dev**: ~$60-85/month
+ - **Staging**: ~$60-85/month  
+ - **Production**: ~$150-500/month (scales with traffic)
+ 
+ ## Need Help?
+ 
+ 1. Check &#96;STEP_BY_STEP_SETUP.md&#96; for detailed instructions
+ 2. Review AWS Console for resource status
+ 3. Check Terraform state: &#96;terraform show&#96;
+ 4. Review GitHub Actions logs
+
```

```diff
- 
+ # 🚀 Start Here: AWS Multi-Environment Setup
+ 
+ ## Quick Answer to Your Questions
+ 
+ ### 1. **Are we going serverless?**
+ **Partially!** We&#39;re using:
+ - ✅ **ECS Fargate** = Serverless containers (no EC2 to manage, auto-scales)
+ - ✅ **RDS** = Managed database (not serverless, but fully managed)
+ - ✅ **ElastiCache** = Managed Redis (not serverless, but fully managed)
+ 
+ **Not fully serverless** (like AWS Lambda), but **serverless containers** which means:
+ - No servers to manage
+ - Auto-scales based on traffic
+ - Pay only for what you use
+ - Still runs your Docker containers
+ 
+ ### 2. **Which services host backend and database?**
+ - **Backend**: **ECS Fargate** (serverless containers)
+ - **Database**: **RDS PostgreSQL** (managed database service)
+ 
+ ### 3. **Is the pipeline accounted for?**
+ ✅ **Yes!** I&#39;ve created:
+ - Multi-environment Terraform structure (dev/staging/prod)
+ - GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline
+ - Environment-specific configurations
+ 
+ ### 4. **Do I need to do manual work in AWS?**
+ **Minimal!** You only need to:
+ 1. Create IAM user (one-time, 5 minutes)
+ 2. Run setup script (automated)
+ 3. Deploy via Terraform (automated)
+ 
+ Everything else is automated through Terraform and GitHub Actions.
+ 
+ ## Your Action Plan
+ 
+ ### ✅ Step 1: Read the Complete Guide
+ Open &#96;STEP_BY_STEP_SETUP.md&#96; - it has everything you need with detailed instructions.
+ 
+ ### ✅ Step 2: Initial AWS Setup (15 minutes)
+ 
+ 1. **Create IAM User** (AWS Console)
+    - IAM → Users → Add user
+    - Name: &#96;predico-terraform&#96;
+    - Access: Programmatic
+    - Permissions: AdministratorAccess
+    - **Save credentials!**
+ 
+ 2. **Configure AWS CLI**
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    aws configure
+    # Enter your IAM user credentials
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 3. **Run Setup Script**
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    cd infrastructure/scripts
+    ./setup-aws.sh
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### ✅ Step 3: Deploy Dev Environment (20 minutes)
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ cd infrastructure/terraform
+ terraform init -backend-config=envs/dev/backend.hcl
+ terraform plan -var-file=envs/dev/terraform.tfvars
+ terraform apply -var-file=envs/dev/terraform.tfvars
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### ✅ Step 4: Set Up CI/CD (10 minutes)
+ 
+ 1. Add GitHub Secrets:
+    - &#96;AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID&#96;
+    - &#96;AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY&#96;
+    - &#96;AWS_ACCOUNT_ID&#96;
+ 
+ 2. Create branches:
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    git checkout -b develop
+    git push -u origin develop
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 3. Push to &#96;develop&#96; → Auto-deploys to dev!
+ 
+ ## Architecture Diagram
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
+ │         GitHub Repository                │
+ │  (main/staging/develop branches)        │
+ └──────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
+                │
+                │ GitHub Actions CI/CD
+                │ (Tests → Build → Deploy)
+                ▼
+ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
+ │              AWS Account                 │
+ │                                          │
+ │  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐    │
+ │  │   Dev Env    │  │ Staging Env  │    │
+ │  │              │  │              │    │
+ │  │ ECS Fargate  │  │ ECS Fargate  │    │
+ │  │ RDS (small)  │  │ RDS (medium) │    │
+ │  │ Redis        │  │ Redis        │    │
+ │  │ ALB          │  │ ALB          │    │
+ │  └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘    │
+ │                                          │
+ │  ┌──────────────┐                       │
+ │  │ Production   │                       │
+ │  │              │                       │
+ │  │ ECS Fargate  │                       │
+ │  │ RDS (large)  │                       │
+ │  │ Redis        │                       │
+ │  │ ALB + Domain │                       │
+ │  └──────────────┘                       │
+ └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## What Gets Created Per Environment
+ 
+ Each environment (dev/staging/prod) gets:
+ - ✅ Separate VPC (isolated network)
+ - ✅ Separate RDS database
+ - ✅ Separate Redis cluster
+ - ✅ Separate ECS cluster
+ - ✅ Separate ALB
+ - ✅ Separate ECR repositories
+ - ✅ Separate S3 buckets
+ - ✅ Separate security groups
+ 
+ **Complete isolation** - no resource sharing between environments!
+ 
+ ## Cost Breakdown
+ 
+ | Environment | Monthly Cost | What You Get |
+ |------------|--------------|--------------|
+ | **Dev** | ~$60-85 | Small instances, single AZ |
+ | **Staging** | ~$60-85 | Medium instances, multi-AZ |
+ | **Production** | ~$150-500 | Large instances, multi-AZ, auto-scaling |
+ 
+ *Costs scale with actual usage*
+ 
+ ## Next Steps
+ 
+ 1. **Read**: &#96;STEP_BY_STEP_SETUP.md&#96; for detailed instructions
+ 2. **Follow**: Phase 1 (Initial AWS Setup)
+ 3. **Deploy**: Dev environment first
+ 4. **Test**: Push to &#96;develop&#96; branch to trigger CI/CD
+ 
+ ## Need Help?
+ 
+ - **Quick Start**: See &#96;QUICK_START.md&#96;
+ - **Detailed Guide**: See &#96;STEP_BY_STEP_SETUP.md&#96;
+ - **Architecture**: See &#96;AWS_SETUP_GUIDE.md&#96;
+ - **Deployment**: See &#96;DEPLOYMENT.md&#96;
+ 
+ ## Important Notes
+ 
+ ⚠️ **Never use root account** - Always use IAM user
+ ⚠️ **Save credentials** - IAM secret keys are shown only once
+ ⚠️ **Review Terraform plan** - Always check before applying
+ ⚠️ **Start with dev** - Test everything in dev before staging/prod
+ 
+ Ready to start? Open &#96;STEP_BY_STEP_SETUP.md&#96; and follow Phase 1!
+ 
```

</details>

</tool-use>
